Astronomy Picture of the Day

Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer.

Noctilucent Clouds over Sweden

Explanation:  Sometimes it’s night on the ground but day in the air. As the Earth rotates to eclipse the Sun,  sunset rises up from the ground. Therefore, at sunset on the ground, sunlight still shines on  clouds  above. Under  usual circumstances , a pretty sunset might be visible, but unusual  noctilucent clouds  float so high up they can be seen well after dark. Normally too dim to be seen,  they  may become visible just after sunset during the summer when illuminated by sunlight from below the horizon.  Noctilucent cloud s are the highest clouds and are known more technically as  polar mesospheric clouds . Featured here as they appeared in early August, a network of blue noctilucent clouds was captured in the distant sky above a field of green grass near  Linköping ,  Sweden , with trees in  stark silhouette  across the horizon. Much about  noctilucent clouds  has been  discovered  only in the past two decades, while  how they form and evolve  remains a topic of  active research .
